comment: Time-boxed exceptions for the production dependency audit gate (npm run audit:ci). Every entry needs a package, a reason, and an expiry date. Expired entries fail CI so the list cannot rot. Document the compensating control in docs/SECURITY.md.

entries.reason: No fixed 1.x exists in the registry (latest is 1.12.2; the advisories reference 1.15.0). The browser client only calls NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, a build-time constant pointing at this hospital's own API; it never accepts a user-supplied URL, proxy, or axios config object. The SSRF/proxy-credential advisories therefore have no attacker-controlled input path. Revisit when 1.15+ is published.

No fixed 4.x is published (latest 4.0.4; the advisory covers <=4.0.5). It is reached only transitively through axios and supertest. The portal builds no multipart bodies from user-controlled field names, and the public forms submit JSON only. Revisit when 4.0.6 is published.

The fix requires zod 4.6.7, which is not published (latest 4.6.5). zod is used only for frontend form validation with bounded string fields; the backend re-validates every request with class-validator DTOs and Joi configuration validation, so an oversized-collection memory DoS cannot cross the trust boundary.

GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828 (trailing bytes after a compressed body) is fixed in body-parser 2.4.0, which is not published (latest 2.3.0). Express 5 requires the 2.x line, so downgrading is not an option. Compensating control: both body parsers are mounted explicitly in src/bootstrap.ts with a 100 kB limit, so the decompressed body a single request can produce is bounded, and the Vercel function is capped at 30 s and 1024 MB. Revisit when 2.4.0 is published.

Reported only transitively: Express 5 is flagged because it depends on the vulnerable body-parser. No advisory names Express itself. The same 100 kB parser limit and 30 s serverless timeout documented for body-parser apply. Tracked through the body-parser entry so it disappears when that upgrade lands.

Aggregate finding: the package is flagged only because it pulls Express 5 and body-parser 2.x. 11.2.5 is the newest release outside the separately flagged `<=11.1.14` and `11.2.6 - 12.0.0-alpha.7` ranges; 12.x would force TypeScript 6. Tracked through the body-parser entry.

The newest advisory (GHSA-q7qp-rjg7-q26m) covers <2.5.0 and 2.5.0 is not published (latest 2.4.0), so no 2.x upgrade clears it and Nest pins multer 2.2.0 exactly. Compensating control: the backend exposes no upload endpoint at all - there is no FileInterceptor, FilesInterceptor or UploadedFile in apps/backend/src - so multer's multipart parser never runs. Revisit when 2.5.0 is published or an upload feature is added.
